{{recipe}}

The acidic, fruity flavor of Pinot Noir perfectly matches the fatty, slightly gamey taste of the duck.

== Ingredients ==
* 4 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (28 [[Cookbook:Oz|oz]]) boneless [[Cookbook:Duck|duck]] breasts
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* Freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]]
* 1 ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] Pinot Noir [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallot]], very finely [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]

== Procedure ==
#Score skin of duck in a diamond pattern, being careful not to cut into the meat. Sprinkle on both sides liberally with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
#Heat a large stainless steel [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over medium high heat. Add 2 duck breasts, skin side down, and cook until skin is golden brown, about 10 minutes. Flip and cook 3 minutes. Move to a greased roasting pan and repeat with remaining duck.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 400°F for 12 minutes for medium rare. Remove and keep warm.
#Pour most of the fat out, leaving 2 tbsp. Place pan back on medium high heat, add shallot, and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] until translucent. [[Cookbook:Deglazing|Deglaze]] pan with wine and ignite carefully with a firestick, if desired. If you ignited it, wait until flames die before continuing. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
#Cook wine until reduced by ⅔. [[Cookbook:Slicing|Slice]] duck on the bias and drizzle with sauce. Serve immediately.

recipe.name: Seared Duck Breast with Pinot Noir Reduction

steps.text: Score skin of duck in a diamond pattern, being careful not to cut into the meat. Sprinkle on both sides liberally with salt and freshly ground black pepper.

Heat a large stainless steel skillet over medium high heat. Add 2 duck breasts, skin side down, and cook until skin is golden brown, about 10 minutes. Flip and cook 3 minutes. Move to a greased roasting pan and repeat with remaining duck.
Bake at 400°F for 12 minutes for medium rare. Remove and keep warm.

Pour most of the fat out, leaving 2 tbsp. Place pan back on medium high heat, add shallot, and sauté until translucent. Deglaze pan with wine and ignite carefully with a firestick, if desired. If you ignited it, wait until flames die before continuing. Bring to a boil.
Cook wine until reduced by ⅔. Slice duck on the bias and drizzle with sauce. Serve immediately.
